name: Copart, Inc.
moat_justification: Dominant salvage-auction marketplace in a structural duopoly with RB Global's IAA: long-term insurer seller relationships, a scarce permitted land bank of 250+ yards near metro areas, and a global buyer network (~1M members in 185+ countries) whose bidding depth raises seller proceeds and locks in assignments. Proven pricing power (revenue per unit rose even as FY2026 volumes fell), asset-light service model, debt-free balance sheet, and high returns on capital held through cycles. Not a 9-10: volume is hostage to insurance claims activity and insurer total-loss behavior, international buyers (38.2% of US units in FY2026) are FX/tariff-sensitive, and RB Global is a credible, consolidating rival.
fragility_flags: WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.0x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Wide-moat (8/10) salvage-auction compounder, but at $26.41 the weighted IRR is 9.4% (IV@15% $13.77) — it only clears Andrew's 15% hurdle at roughly $13.77 or below.
moat_for: Salvage duopoly with RB Global/IAA; dominant share of insurer salvage assignments
Scarce, permitted land bank — 250+ locations near metro areas, hard to replicate
Global buyer network (~1M members, 185+ countries) deepens bids and seller proceeds
Proven pricing power — revenue per unit rose while FY2026 volumes fell
Asset-light service model; debt-free with large net cash
moat_against: Volumes hostage to insurance claims activity and insurer total-loss thresholds
Insurer concentration — a few large carriers drive assignment flow
International buyers bought 38.2% of US units in FY2026 — FX/tariff sensitive
RB Global/IAA is a credible consolidating rival
ACV integration and dealer-channel expansion is unproven for Copart
